visuals.title: Where an URTI sits
visuals.text: Nose, sinuses, pharynx and larynx: everything above the vocal cords and trachea.

glossary.Pharynx: The throat behind the mouth and nose.
glossary.Larynx: The voice box, at the top of the trachea.
glossary.Nasal congestion: Blocked or stuffy nose from swollen lining.
glossary.Low-grade fever: A mildly raised temperature, roughly 37.5 to 38°C.
glossary.Influenza: Flu virus: causes fever, aches and respiratory symptoms, sometimes severe.
glossary.Coronavirus: A family of viruses causing colds, and also COVID-19.
glossary.Laryngeal obstruction: Narrowing or blockage at the voice box, causing stridor.
glossary.Pneumonia: Infection of the lung air sacs (alveoli) causing consolidation.
glossary.Nasal decongestants: Sprays or tablets that shrink swollen nasal blood vessels to unblock the nose.
glossary.Penicillin V: Phenoxymethylpenicillin, an oral penicillin used for throat and sinus infections.
glossary.Mucosa: The moist lining of the airways.
glossary.Oedema: Swelling caused by fluid in the tissues.
glossary.Laryngotracheal: Relating to the larynx and trachea.
glossary.Subglottic narrowing: Narrowing of the airway just below the vocal cords.
glossary.Middle ear: The air-filled space behind the eardrum, linked to the throat by the Eustachian tube.
glossary.Host immune response: The body's own defence that clears the infection.
glossary.Sneezing: A forceful reflex burst of air through the nose to clear irritants.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used for pain, fever and inflammation.
glossary.Self-care: Managing symptoms at home with rest, fluids and simple painkillers.
glossary.Chest X-ray: Plain X-ray of the chest; used here to look for pneumonia.
